annotationRationale: Both methods establish a universal lower bound and provide a four-guess construction attaining it. The arguments use concrete grid positions without requiring a separate graph-theory framework.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate for this discrete extremal counting problem; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The minimum is 4, choice C. Four disjoint possible placements defeat any three guesses along an all-miss path, while guessing the four side-middle squares meets every placement. The stem, choices and key agree; no figure is required or supplied.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: For 2023_AMC_10B_Q10, disjoint-rectangles-and-coloring and count-rectangle-positions are both retained and independently valid. The historical disjoint-domino-packing route is merged into the first method. The historical nonadjacent-unguessed-cells route has no supplied worked explanation and is omitted as an equivalent complementary formulation: the same packing bounds nonadjacent unguessed cells by five. No useful distinct reviewed route is missing.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed extremal node matches both universal lower bounds and attaining constructions. Removing graph-models from question support is justified because neither explanation requires an explicit graph framework.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is appropriate for this discrete extremal counting problem; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: All four listed pairs are adjacent and mutually disjoint. Three guesses touch at most three pairs, leaving a placement consistent with three misses, including for adaptive strategies. Every allowed rectangle contains exactly one of squares 2,4,6,8, so four guesses suffice.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Reuse of 2023_AMC_10B_Q10/disjoint-rectangles-and-coloring is accurately identified. Both inherited reference IDs, live-reference-2023_AMC_10B_Q10 and aops-reference-2023_AMC_10B_Q10, are retained. The project explanation is permitted reuse, with source-informed-original status and no official MAA claim.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The labeling makes the disjoint placements reconstructible without a diagram. The explanation clearly separates necessity from sufficiency and explicitly handles adaptive guessing.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:extremal-principle precisely describes the lower-bound argument and matching construction.

methodReviews.mathCheck: There are 12 placements. Without a center guess, three guesses eliminate at most 9. With a center guess, its four placements plus at most two remaining placements per other guess eliminate at most 8. Thus a consistent placement survives either case. The four side-middle guesses meet every placement, proving 4.
